answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock scarce tokens before it may post jobs or claim rewards, with the bond slashed when independently verifiable evidence shows fraud. One operator can still create many identities, but each must tie up capital, and repeated attacks multiply the cost while leaving honest agents’ bonds intact. If rewards arrive slowly, the attacker also pays the opportunity cost of funds locked beyond the horizon of a quick exploit—more like diverting a river than borrowing from an ocean.
